history.hpi: Onset of epigastric burning and mid-back discomfort approximately 45 minutes prior to EMS arrival while eating dinner; associated diaphoresis, nausea, and mild dyspnea. Patient initially attributed symptoms to heartburn and took antacids without relief. Denies classic substernal chest pressure or radiation to the left arm.
history.lastOralIntake: Dinner (roast beef sandwich) approximately 1 hour prior to symptom onset
history.events: Patient was eating dinner when he developed burning epigastric and mid-back discomfort; took OTC antacid tablets with no relief. Wife called 911 after roughly 45 minutes when he became visibly diaphoretic and pale.

scene.dispatch: Medic 4, respond to 4417 Birchwood Lane for a 60-year-old male with stomach discomfort and nausea, patient conscious and breathing.
scene.location: Single-family home, seated at the kitchen table
scene.bystanders: Wife present; states husband has been rubbing his chest and back and sweating for the last 45 minutes, thought it was indigestion
visualCues: Patient seated at the kitchen table, diaphoretic and pale
Half-empty bottle of antacid tablets on the table
Patient periodically grimacing and shifting position, rubbing mid-back

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Patient is alert and conversant, complaining of epigastric burning and mid-back discomfort he attributes to indigestion. He is diaphoretic, pale, and mildly tachypneic. Nothing about the presentation screams 'chest pain,' which is exactly the trap of a posterior STEMI equivalent.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mildly increased rate, no accessory muscle use, lungs clear bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, strong and slightly rapid; skin pale, cool, diaphoretic
otherFindings: Rates discomfort 6/10, describes as burning/pressure in epigastrium radiating to mid-back
Denies typical substernal chest pain or left arm radiation
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I think it's just my stomach, I get heartburn all the time, but this feels different, kind of in my back too."

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform focused history/physical; recognize atypical anginal-equivalent symptoms (epigastric/back pain, diaphoresis) as possible ACS
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Chest pain or discomfort in other areas of the body (e.g., arm, jaw, epigastrium) of suspected cardiac origin, shortness of breath, associated or unexplained sweating, nausea, vomiting, or dizziness. Atypical or unusual symptoms are more common in women, the elderly, and diabetic patients.
expectedActions.rationale: Posterior STEMI classically presents with vague epigastric/back discomfort rather than classic substernal chest pain, and is frequently misattributed to GI causes.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The 12-lead EKG is the primary diagnostic tool that identifies a STEMI; it is imperative that EMS clinicians routinely acquire a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes for all patients exhibiting signs and symptoms of ACS.
expectedActions.rationale: Early 12-lead acquisition is the only way to catch the ST depression V1-V3/tall R wave pattern that signals a posterior STEMI equivalent.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

transitions.condition: Crew acquires 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes, recognizes ST depression in V1-V3 with tall, broad R waves as a posterior STEMI equivalent, and obtains posterior leads (V7-V9) which confirm ST elevation.

transitions.if: Posterior STEMI missed, treated as reflux
transitions.condition: Crew attributes the presentation to indigestion/GERD, does not obtain posterior leads or recognize the ST depression V1-V3 with tall R wave pattern as a posterior STEMI equivalent, and no STEMI activation is made.

phases.name: Posterior STEMI recognized
phases.description: Posterior STEMI equivalent confirmed; crew proceeds with STEMI protocol treatment and hospital notification.
phases.triggerCondition: Initial 12-lead shows ST depression greater than 0.5 mm in leads V1-V3 with tall, broad R waves and upright T waves - a mirror-image pattern of posterior injury. Crew places posterior leads V7-V9, which reveal ST elevation confirming posterior STEMI.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mildly increased rate, no accessory muscle use, lungs clear bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, strong and rapid; skin pale, cool, diaphoretic
otherFindings: 12-lead: ST depression V1-V3 with tall R waves and upright T waves
Posterior leads V7-V9 show ST elevation, confirming posterior STEMI
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It's still there, right in the middle of my back and up under my ribs."

expectedActions.shortAction: Obtain posterior leads (V7-V9); initial EKG is non-diagnostic in appearance but suspicious
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Performance of serial EKGs is encouraged for symptomatic patients with EKGs initially non-diagnostic for STEMI.
expectedActions.rationale: Posterior leads reveal the ST elevation that is 'mirrored' as ST depression on the standard anterior leads V1-V3.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Activate STEMI system of care; give advance notification to receiving PCI-capable hospital
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Advance notification should be provided to the receiving hospital for patients identified as having a STEMI.
expectedActions.rationale: Minimizing first-medical-contact-to-balloon time is the single biggest driver of myocardial salvage.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer aspirin; chewable, non-enteric-coated aspirin preferred (162-325 mg).
expectedActions.rationale: Antiplatelet therapy limits thrombus propagation in ACS.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.rationale: Vascular access needed for medications and to manage hemodynamic changes.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL (SBP 122 mmHg, above 100 mmHg threshold); may repeat q3-5 min; screened negative for PDE5 inhibitor use
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual (SL), can repeat q (quaque, every) 3-5 minutes if SBP greater than 100 mmHg. The use of nitrates should be avoided in any patient who has used a phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours.
expectedActions.rationale: Nitrates reduce preload/afterload and can relieve ischemic discomfort; PDE5 inhibitor use must be excluded first to avoid refractory hypotension.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Continue cardiac monitoring; watch for dysrhythmias or clinical deterioration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Observe for signs of clinical deterioration: dysrhythmias, chest pain, shortness of breath, decreased level of consciousness/syncope, or other signs of shock/hypotension.
expectedActions.rationale: Posterior STEMI carries risk of dysrhythmia and hemodynamic compromise; continuous monitoring catches deterioration early.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

transitions.condition: Aspirin given, IV established, nitroglycerin administered for persistent discomfort after PDE5 screening, and STEMI activation transmitted to the receiving facility.

phases.name: STEMI activated, transport to PCI center
phases.description: Patient packaged for transport; repeat 12-lead performed en route showing persistent posterior injury pattern; hospital catheterization lab activated.
phases.triggerCondition: Aspirin administered, IV established, nitroglycerin given for persistent discomfort, and STEMI activation transmitted; crew transports emergently to the nearest PCI-capable facility with serial EKG monitoring.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Normal rate and depth, lungs clear bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, strong and regular; skin improving color, still mildly diaphoretic
otherFindings: Repeat 12-lead/posterior leads show persistent posterior injury pattern
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's a lot better, still feel a little pressure but nothing like before."

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs en route; reassess for interval changes
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs (especially if clinical changes are noted).
expectedActions.rationale: Serial EKGs document evolution of the injury pattern and catch new dysrhythmias or extension of infarct.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide early notification to receiving facility of any changes in patient condition or serial EKGs
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Early notification to receiving facility of any changes in patient condition or serial EKGs.
expectedActions.rationale: Keeps the cath lab team updated so they can prepare for arrival.
expectedActions.protocolReference: MATC: Chest Pain/Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS)/ST-segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 95 mcg IV (95 kg x 1 mcg/kg = 95 mcg; max initial dose 100 mcg) for discomfort unresponsive to nitrates
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg).
expectedActions.rationale: ACS protocol allows opiate analgesia as an alternative when pain is unresponsive to nitrates; dosed and capped per the Pain Management guideline.

phases.name: Posterior STEMI missed
phases.description: Without recognition of the posterior STEMI pattern, the patient's ongoing ischemia worsens over the next several minutes; discomfort intensifies and he becomes more diaphoretic and anxious.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew attributes the epigastric/back discomfort to indigestion; the 12-lead shows ST depression V1-V3 with tall R waves but this is not recognized as a posterior STEMI mirror pattern. Posterior leads are not obtained and no STEMI activation is made, so the ongoing ischemia progresses untreated.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Increased rate, mild accessory muscle use
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present, weak and rapid; skin pale, cool, profusely diaphoretic
otherFindings: No STEMI activation made; patient still believed to have GI upset
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Something's not right, it's getting a lot worse, I feel like I can't catch my breath."

transitions.condition: Approximately 5 minutes after worsening symptoms with no STEMI treatment or activation, the patient becomes unresponsive and pulseless as untreated posterior ischemia precipitates ventricular fibrillation.

phases.name: VF arrest - missed STEMI
phases.description: Cardiac arrest secondary to acute ischemia; crew must immediately recognize arrest and begin high-quality CPR with defibrillation.
phases.triggerCondition: Approximately 5 minutes after onset of worsening symptoms, the patient becomes unresponsive and pulseless; the monitor reveals coarse ventricular fibrillation secondary to unrecognized and untreated posterior STEMI.

otherFindings: No palpable pulse on primary survey

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize cardiac arrest; begin immediate high-quality chest compressions
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Initiate chest compressions in cases with no bystander chest compressions or take over compressions from bystanders while a second rescuer is setting up the AED or defibrillator.
expectedActions.rationale: Prompt compressions maintain coronary and cerebral perfusion until defibrillation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Defibrillate at 120 J (Zoll biphasic) as soon as VF is confirmed
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Zoll i. Adult - 120 J, 150 J, 200 J.
expectedActions.rationale: Defibrillation is the only definitive treatment for VF.

expectedActions.shortAction: Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO push (95 kg x 0.1 mg/kg = 9.5 mg, capped at protocol max 1 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer epinephrine (0.1 mg/kg, maximum dose 1 mg) IV/IO during the first or second round of compressions.
expectedActions.rationale: Epinephrine improves coronary perfusion pressure during CPR.

expectedActions.shortAction: Resume chest compressions immediately post-shock without a pulse check, for 2 minutes
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Chest compressions should resume immediately after defibrillation attempts with no pauses for pulse checks for 2 minutes regardless of the rhythm displayed on the cardiac monitor.
